about: Part of the reference catalogue: designed experiments from Chapter 5 (Process Improvement) of the NIST/SEMATECH
e-Handbook of Statistical Methods. Each worked example with data is an experiment (its runs and responses, from
the page or the data file it links); each design a page prints or specifies is a design. expected: every number,
alias, generator and run list the pages print about them, with where (the section, the page's URL, the kind of
source: text, table, Dataplot or R output, figure, data file or design table, and a quotation) and a check. The
handbook numbers factors 1, 2, 3, ..., and those digits name the factors of the fractions here (factor 10 and
up become letters, as each entry's notes say). Read with process_improve.experiments.reference_catalogue.

experiments.name: nist-5-4-7-1-ceramic-strength
experiments.title: Strength of sintered reaction-bonded silicon nitride against five machining factors: a 2^5 full factorial

factors.name: X2
factors.description: Down feed rate: slow and fast

responses.name: strength
responses.description: Mean (over 15 repetitions) of the ceramic strength

responses.name: new_strength
responses.description: Y:NewStrength, the Box-Cox transform of strength with lambda = 0.2 the page uses: (y^0.2 - 1) / (0.2 gm^(0.2 - 1)), gm the geometric mean of the 32 strengths; computed here, not printed

design.details: no centre runs; the page prints the runs in standard order with their randomized run order

runs.notes: The page's table, in standard order, identical to https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/datasets/CERAMIC.DAT (columns X1 to X5, Y, ORDER). order is the randomized run order. new_strength is computed from strength with the page's Box-Cox formula (pri471_eq1.gif) and lambda = 0.2, as the R code computes newstrength.

experiments.notes: The page's coding: X1 -1 = 0.025 m/s, X2 -1 = 0.05 mm, X3 -1 = 140/170, X4 -1 = longitudinal, X5 -1 = batch 1 (the page's optimum and its remark that the first batch is stronger). The ANOVA tables of the page and of the R code are type I sums of squares, which for this orthogonal design equal the library's type II. In the 11-effect model the page prints X1·X2, X1·X3, X1·X4, X2·X4 and X3·X4 with signs opposite to the fit (and to the R code's summary.lm, captured beside them), while X1·X2·X4 agrees; the effect sizes and p-values all agree.

experiments.name: nist-5-4-7-2-catapult
experiments.title: Distance a catapult throws a ball against five factors: a 2^(5-1) resolution V with four centre runs

factors.name: h
factors.description: Band height: height of the pivot point for the rubber bands

factors.name: s
factors.description: Start angle: where the operator releases the arm

factors.name: l
factors.description: Arm length: distance the arm is extended

factors.name: e
factors.description: Stop angle: where the forward motion of the arm stops

responses.name: distance
responses.description: Distance from the front of the catapult to where the plastic golf ball lands

responses.name: ln_distance
responses.description: Natural logarithm of distance, the response of the page's step 3a; computed here, not printed

design.type: 2^(5-1) resolution V fractional factorial with 4 centre runs
design.details: E = ABCD (stop angle = height x start x bands x length in the coded settings); the number of bands is discrete, so the centre runs are two with one band and two with two

runs.notes: The page's table in run order (distance, height, start, bands, length, stop, order), identical to https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/datasets/CATAPULT.DAT, which lists the runs in Yates order with the coded columns X1 to X5 the analysis uses ('the orthogonally coded columns'); h, s, b, l, e here are those coded columns. The centre runs have b = -1 (one band, runs 7 and 19) or +1 (two bands, runs 2 and 13), the other four factors 0. ln_distance is computed from distance, as the R code's logdist.

experiments.notes: The factor names are the page's abbreviations: Height (h), Start (s), Bands (b), Length (l), Stop (e). The page's description gives band height levels of 2.25 and 4.75 inches with a centre of 3.5, and the data file's header says the same, but every printed run is at 3.25, 4 or 4.75 inches; the printed stop-angle centre is 62 degrees, not the 62.5 midway between 45 and 80. The coded columns, which the fits use, are -1, 0, +1 throughout. Lack of fit is tested against pure error from the two pairs of centre runs (one pair per number of bands), 2 degrees of freedom, as the R code's lof factor groups them.

factors.name: H2WF6
factors.description: Ratio of the gaseous reactants H2 and WF6 (H2/WF6)

responses.name: uniformity
responses.description: Standard deviation over the mean of 49 sheet-resistance measurements across a wafer; lower is better

responses.name: stress
responses.description: Layer stress, from an optical measurement of wafer bow; lower is better

design.type: central composite inscribed design with 3 centre runs
design.details: axial runs at the range limits (coded +/-1) and corners at +/-0.71; Experiment 2 of Czitrom and Spagon (1997), chapter 15

runs.notes: The page's table in run order, identical to https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/datasets/IMPROVE-5_4_7_3.DAT; Pressure and H2WF6 are the page's coded columns, as printed (corners at +/-0.71, a rounding of 1/sqrt(2) = 0.7071), with which the page's coded fits reproduce; with the exact 0.7071 they do not.

experiments.notes: The page prints its fits in coded units, on the printed coded columns; the R code linked from the page fits the same models in natural units (torr and ratio), whose coding of the corners is exact, so its R-squared, residual standard errors and sums of squares differ slightly from the page's: they are captured in the entry nist-5-4-7-3-cvd-tungsten-natural-units. The page's full quadratic fit of Stress squares H2/WF6 in natural units (2 to 10) and codes every other column: so fitted, the printed runs reproduce its table exactly, and its model comparison (0.029804, 0.00596, 2.08) follows from that fit; the checks fit the coded square the table names and record the difference.

experiments.name: nist-5-4-7-3-cvd-tungsten-natural-units
experiments.title: The CVD tungsten experiment of 5.4.7.3 as its R code fits it: pressure and H2/WF6 in natural units

factors.name: H2WF6
factors.description: Ratio of the gaseous reactants H2 and WF6 (H2/WF6)

responses.name: uniformity
responses.description: Standard deviation over the mean of 49 sheet-resistance measurements across a wafer

responses.name: stress
responses.description: Layer stress, from an optical measurement of wafer bow

design.type: central composite inscribed design with 3 centre runs

runs.notes: The natural settings of the page's table and of https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/datasets/IMPROVE-5_4_7_3.DAT, which the R code reads; coded here from 4 to 80 torr and 2 to 10, a linear change of units, so every statistic that does not depend on the units (residuals, sums of squares, R-squared, F and p) is the R code's.

experiments.notes: The R code fits polynomials in the natural units, so its coefficients and their standard errors are per torr and per unit of ratio, which the library's coded fits do not report; those are not captured. Its ANOVA tables are sequential (type I), which here equal the library's type II: pressure and H2/WF6 are orthogonal in this design, and pressure is orthogonal to its square once centred.
